A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UniRec research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices support comparison. Appendices A–F are retained, with Appendix G added in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original recommendation experiments on Beauty, Baby and Yelp, including benchmark comparisons, component ablations and token-count sensitivity results in Tables 2–3 and Figures 2–3.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds baseline comparisons, full-catalog ranking, modality-removal tests, representation diagnostics and computational measurements in Sections 4.2–4.4 and Appendix G.

M1.justification: The specified image encoder changes from CLIP ViT-L/14 to ViT-B/32, with the projection input in Section 3.1 changing from 768 to 512 dimensions. Triplet fusion, hierarchical aggregation, losses and ranking remain unchanged. v3's new statement that modality encoders remain frozen throughout training conflicts with its retained encoder-pretraining description, so a further training-procedure change cannot be established.

E1.justification: Beauty, Baby and Yelp next-item recommendation remain the benchmark coverage. v3 adds controlled input conditions with individual image, numerical, textual or categorical modality groups missing (Table 4). Full-catalog ranking and the 2,000-item beauty-domain representation analysis expand procedures and analyses without establishing a new application domain.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds evaluated MLLMRec and NoteLLM-2 comparisons across all three datasets; these works were already cited but lacked result rows in v1. This substantially broadens the evaluated LLM alternatives to native multimodal prompting and multimodal representation learning. Table 5 also introduces explicit text-only LLM configurations as efficiency comparators.

E3.justification: v3 supplements the retained 99-negative evaluation with full-catalog ranking over 12,101 Beauty items. It adds representation diagnostics on 2,000 items using effective rank, reconstruction similarity and neighborhood overlap, plus latency/memory protocols with varying token counts and batch sizes on an A100 using bfloat16. These are substantial additions to evaluation design; the original filtering, history length and sampled-ranking protocol remain.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component, fusion-family and token-count ablations, v3 tests addition against Concat+MLP and gated triplet fusion, systematically removes modality groups, compares fusion behavior under missing text, and examines raw versus Q-Former representations. Full-catalog evaluation checks sampling sensitivity, while Section 4.4 and Appendix G.4 add computational profiling.

E5.justification: Appendix G.4 newly specifies that latency measurements average 50 forward passes after 10 warmup iterations. This adds a timing-estimation procedure, not evidence of increased training repetitions. Neither version reports accuracy variability across seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: The original Table 2–3 scores and Figures 2–3 are retained, but substantial results are added. Table 11 reports full-catalog Beauty MRR of 0.0552 for UniRec, 0.0483 for LGMRec and 0.0431 for MLLM-MSR. New gated fusion slightly exceeds default UniRec, including Beauty MRR 0.3748 versus 0.3737. Additional tables report new comparator scores, modality sensitivity, representation diagnostics and computational costs; these are not same-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: The problem definitions, triplet summation, hierarchical aggregation, training objectives and appendix attention formula retain their mathematical substance. v3 numbers existing equations and adds empirical or intuitive explanations, but introduces no new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: four-modality encoding, schema-aware triplets and hierarchical Q-Formers for recommendation. Both abstracts retain the claim of improvements up to 15%. The additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining their central scope.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive explanations involving near-orthogonal triplet components, additive fusion under missing inputs, numerical continuity, Q-Former representation transformation and compression-based efficiency. The clean-schema and offline-evaluation limitations remain unchanged. Its new numerical-encoder discussion describes Pure Text as serializing all attributes, conflicting with the retained definition that it discards nontext modalities.

D1.justification: Appendix G.4 substantially expands documentation with component parameter/trainability breakdowns, Q-Former depth and query count, offline precomputation, training-only head handling, PyTorch/precision details and stage-specific budgets and costs. The Hugging Face link changes from a collection to a dataset, while the GitHub link remains. v1's future-code-release statement is removed; these disclosures do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: v3 adds Krichene and Rendle (2020) in connection with sampled evaluation. It expands discussion of the already-cited MLLMRec and NoteLLM-2, including architectural comparisons and an explicit claim of complementary, backbone-independent contributions in Appendix G.2. The broader related-work narrative remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. v3 adds localized method explanations, Section 4.4 and Appendix G, updates author/publication information, adds acknowledgments, and removes the ethics and reproducibility statements. The added scientific material does not amount to a wholesale rewrite of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v3 expands Tables 2–3 and adds eight tables covering the new analyses; the original dataset tables are retained as Tables 6–10. Figure 1 corrects the item-level output label from User Tokens to Item Tokens, while Figures 2–3 retain their plotted content. The publication template substantially changes front matter, typography, margins and figure/table placement.

improvement.justification: The added MLLMRec/NoteLLM-2 comparisons and full-catalog Beauty evaluation address weaknesses in v1's narrower, sampled-only assessment, while computational and implementation details make the paper more informative. The net gain is limited by conflicting encoder-training descriptions and the inconsistent Pure Text interpretation. Table 3 also retains incorrect best-result highlighting after adding numerically stronger gated-fusion results. These reporting problems limit the benefit of the expanded evidence.
